name: manual_ba06d8
claim: On Darwin the loser of two concurrent openat(dir_fd, name, O_CREAT) calls on the same new name gets a spurious ENOENT even though the directory exists (absolute paths and Linux are unaffected); retry once without O_CREAT to open what the rival made, keep the ownership and mode checks on the returned descriptor, and cover it with an injected-ENOENT test because Linux CI can never reproduce the race.

decisions.notes: phylax PR#11 2026-10-13: test_two_workers_can_bootstrap_from_an_empty_state_directory failed 100% on macOS even on the PR's own unmerged tip but passed on Linux CI, so it shipped unnoticed. Reproduced with bare O_RDWR|O_CREAT and a dir_fd; 300/300 loser ENOENT; absolute path 0 failures. Retry shapes (without O_CREAT, with O_CREAT, 4-loop) all measured 0 failures at 16 threads versus ~31% without, so the choice rested on semantics. A bounded single retry plus three deterministic injected tests (retry-once, unsafe-file-still-refused, vanished-dir-not-looped) make the behaviour testable on any OS.
